newsitem.title: USA: NASD fines Calif. muni firm for late G-37 report.
newsitem.headline: NASD fines Calif. muni firm for late G-37 report.

text.p: NASD said Tuesday it fined a California bond firm and its president $20,250 for maintaining inadequate net capital and for not filing a quarterly political contributions report to the MSRB on time.
The National Association of Securities Dealers said Amerivet-Dymally Securities, Inc. of Inglewood and Elton Johnson, Jr. agreed to settle the charges without admitting or denying the allegations.

NASD said the firm underwrote four lease revenue bond deals for California's public works board in 1994 and 1995 without having the $100,000 minimum net capital required by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
NASD said the net capital deficiency was as high as $41,809 at one point.
The firm also failed to report the four deals in a "timely" manner to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board under that panel's rule G-37, NASD said.
Enacted in April 1994, rule G-37 bars muni dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
Dealers must notify MSRB quarterly if they had any reportable contributions or if they did negotiated business during the three-month period.
NASD said it suspended the firm from securities underwriting for 30 days and ordered Johnson to requalify by exam as a financial principal.
